messages.author: e1b933a0d5bbe14f
messages.subject: Freeware spell check list?
parts:
Hello again.

I'd like to make a list of words in my corpus that do not appear in an English dictionary. Is it possible to use the spellcheck from Open Office for this purpose? or is there some other list that will do?

I'm using Linux and still relatively new to it.

messages.author: 7c31dd3eaed5edbe
messages.subject: Re: Freeware spell check list?
parts:
Great idea. However, how do you convert the .oxt file into a .txt file
that can be loaded into R? I downloaded "en_US.oxt" from

http://extensions.services.openoffice.org/en/project/en_US-dict

but when I scanned it into R with the encoding argument as "UTF-8" and
then later as "latin1" it doesn't come thru correctly. When I try to
open it in OOo, it wants to install the dictionary rather than open
the text so that I can save it as a .txt file. Any ideas? Thanks. Earl
Brown

messages.author: e1b933a0d5bbe14f
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: Freeware spell check list?
parts: Right. I used the *.dic file and it loaded right away. I stripped out the numbers and the / and \ symbols. Unfortunately, those seem to tell OO how to construct lemmas so I was left being able to check only base forms. A little inconvenient but the resulting list wasn't too long so I could skim for the info I wanted (which was Romanized/transliterated words in a learner corpus).
